title: feat(grid): compute all eleven spec column summary aggregations (#2890)
body:
Closes the `useColumnSummary` items tracked in #2890.

## The gap

`ColumnSummarySchema` accepts eleven aggregation names. `useColumnSummary` computed five. The other six — `none`, `count_empty`, `count_filled`, `count_unique`, `percent_empty`, `percent_filled` — **passed validation at authoring time and then rendered a blank footer cell**, with no error raised on either side.

objectstack#3761 widened the reachable surface: it promoted the `{ type, field }` object form into the spec, and that form's `type` reuses this same enum.

## What changed

The computation now splits into two families:

- **count/percent** read *raw* cell values, before the numeric parse. So `count_unique` works on text, select and lookup columns, and a value that does not parse as a number still counts as a filled row.
- **sum/avg/min/max** keep the existing numeric parse and column formatting.

A cell is empty when it is `null`, `undefined`, `""` or an empty array — the convention already used by audit history display and form dirty-checking — so an unset multi-select reads as empty rather than as a filled `[]`. `count_unique` keys objects and arrays **by value**; a raw `Set` compares by reference and would call every row distinct.

### Two behavior changes fall out of the enum carrying both names

- **`count` is now every row.** `count_filled` is the non-empty variant, and with both in the enum they cannot mean the same thing. Existing tests use data whose rows are all filled, so they do not distinguish the two; the only column that renders differently than before is one whose values are all empty.
- **A zero count renders `Empty: 0`** instead of collapsing to a blank cell. Zero is the answer to "how many are empty", not the absence of one — the old `count > 0 ? count : null` swallowed it.

### Formatting

Column currency/percent formatting is now gated to the numeric family in one place, rather than the scattered `type !== 'count'` guards. Without this, `count_unique` on a currency column would render `$3.00` instead of `Unique: 3`.

### `none`

`none` and unrecognized names skip the entry entirely instead of registering a blank one, so a view whose columns all opt out renders **no footer row** rather than an empty one.

## Types

The objectui-local `{ type, field }` arm of `ListColumnSchema` was stuck at the same five names, which left the per-column `field` override unavailable for the six new aggregations. It now takes its vocabulary from `SpecColumnSummarySchema` by reference, so the shorthand and the object form cannot accept different names — and the delta drops to zero when that spec release lands and the `.extend()` goes away.

## Removed: the second `useColumnSummary`

`@object-ui/react` exported a hook of the same name with **no callers anywhere in the repo**. Not a duplicate implementation so much as a competing one:

- a different API — `(data, config, locale)` against the grid's `(columns, data, fieldMetadata)` — and a colliding `ColumnSummaryConfig` export of a different shape;
- a doc comment claiming it implements "ColumnSummarySchema from `@objectstack/spec` v2.0.7", six majors behind;
- a `distinct` aggregation **not in the spec vocabulary at all** — the spec calls that `count_unique`.

That last point is why it was worth removing rather than leaving inert: a publicly exported name the spec does not define is the second de-facto contract Commandment #0.1 warns about, and the parity guard below does not reach it.

## Anti-drift guard

New `summary-spec-parity.test.ts` asserts the renderer's supported set equals the spec enum **in both directions**:

- a spec name the renderer omits is the bug this PR fixes;
- a renderer name the spec omits would be local dialect (Commandment #0).

Both new tests were verified against a deliberately broken implementation rather than assumed to work:

| Sabotage | Result |
|---|---|
| Roll the vocabulary back to the original 5 | parity test lists the 5 unimplemented names |
| Make `count_unique` compare by reference | array-by-value case fails (`expected 2 to be 1`) |

## Docs

Per Commandment #2. The footer summary was **undocumented in both** the package README and the plugin docs page; both now carry the full eleven-value table, the emptiness rule, and the formatting boundary.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| unit project (full) | 271 files / 3703 tests pass |
| DOM project (full) | 349 files / 3793 tests pass |
| new summary tests | 55 DOM + 26 unit pass |
| `type-check` (types + plugin-grid) | pass |
| lint | 0 errors; new code contributes no `any` |
| clean rebuild of `@object-ui/react` after the removal | pass, no stale exports |

`@objectstack/spec` added as a **devDependency** of plugin-grid for the parity test — six other `plugin-*` packages already depend on it.

## Noted, not changed

The footer renders `{col.header}: {summary.label}` while the label already carries its own prefix, producing `Amount: Sum: 600`. Pre-existing, and changing it is a design decision rather than a bug fix.
